`Policy.TimeoutAsync` has no production caller in `src/Polly` other than its own overloads. The only other callers are three documentation snippets. I did this with text searches, not by building a call graph, and I changed no files.

`Policy.TimeoutAsync<TResult>` has 24 overloads in `src/Polly/Timeout/AsyncTimeoutTResultSyntax.cs`. The non-generic `Policy.TimeoutAsync` has a parallel set in `AsyncTimeoutSyntax.cs`. The two sets do not call each other.

## Production methods that reach the generic `Policy.TimeoutAsync<TResult>`

**Overloads that delegate to other overloads** (`AsyncTimeoutTResultSyntax.cs`):
- The `int seconds` overloads, which take an optional `TimeoutStrategy` and optional `onTimeoutAsync` handler (3-arg and 4-arg forms). They call the `Func<Context, TimeSpan>` overloads at lines 15, 29, 46, 66, 84 and 105.
- The `TimeSpan timeout` overloads, same variants. They call the `Func<Context, TimeSpan>` overloads at lines 118, 132, 148, 168, 186 and 206.
- The `Func<TimeSpan> timeoutProvider` overloads, same variants. They call the `Func<Context, TimeSpan>` overloads at lines 223, 241, 261, 281, 302 and 323.
- The `Func<Context, TimeSpan> timeoutProvider` overloads without a handler, or with the 3-arg handler. They funnel into the 4-arg overload: line 391 is explicit, and the expression-bodied overloads at lines 333–370 reach it the same way.

Every one of these ends at the final overload, `Policy.TimeoutAsync<TResult>(Func<Context, TimeSpan>, TimeoutStrategy, Func<Context, TimeSpan, Task, Exception, Task>)` at line 405. That overload constructs `AsyncTimeoutPolicy<TResult>` at line 417.

**Callers outside the overloads:** the only ones are in `src/Snippets/Docs`, which are documentation snippets and not shipped library code:
- `Migration.Timeout_V7` calls the generic version (`Policy.TimeoutAsync<HttpResponseMessage>`) and also the non-generic `Policy.TimeoutAsync`.
- `Migration.SafeExecute_V7` calls the generic version twice (`<int>`).
- `Migration.PolicyWrap_V7` calls only the non-generic `Policy.TimeoutAsync`.

Nothing else in `src` references it. The matches in `AsyncTimeoutPolicy.cs` and `AsyncTimeoutEngine.cs` are only `onTimeoutAsync` parameters and fields. The `Polly.Core` tests, the extensions tests and `TestUtilities.cs` have no `\bTimeoutAsync\b` match, so no further tests reach it.

## Test files that exercise it

- `test/Polly.Specs/Timeout/TimeoutTResultAsyncSpecs.cs`: generic `TimeoutAsync<TResult>`, 96 references.
- `test/Polly.Specs/Timeout/TimeoutOverloadSmokeSpecs.cs`: 11 `TimeoutAsync<` references, plus non-generic ones.
- `test/Polly.Specs/Timeout/TimeoutAsyncSpecs.cs`: the non-generic overloads only, 105 references.
- `test/Polly.Specs/IAsyncPolicyExtensionsSpecs.cs`: one non-generic call, `Policy.TimeoutAsync(10)`.

If you meant the non-generic `Policy.TimeoutAsync` from `AsyncTimeoutSyntax.cs`, the answer has the same shape. Its 24 overloads funnel into the final overload at line 376 (`Func<Context, TimeSpan>`, `TimeoutStrategy`, 4-arg handler), which constructs `AsyncTimeoutPolicy`. The snippet callers are `Migration.Timeout_V7`, `Migration.PolicyWrap_V7` and `Migration.SafeExecute_V7`, and the test files are as listed above.
